original_text: We will extract fixed contextual embeddings from various layers of the pre-trained model and feed them into a BiLSTM classifier, comparing its performance to the standard fine-tuning approach.
modified_text: We will extract fixed contextual embeddings from various layers of the pre-trained model and feed them into a minimal, single-layer BiLSTM classifier with a hidden size of 64. This simple setup will be used to isolate the raw power of the embeddings when compared to the standard fine-tuning approach.
explanation: This error introduces a confounding variable by specifying a deliberately underpowered model for the feature-based approach. A single-layer BiLSTM with a small hidden size of 64 is likely insufficient for a complex task like NER. While the justification of "isolating the raw power of the embeddings" sounds plausible, it creates an unfair comparison. The fine-tuning approach utilizes the full, large, pre-trained model, whereas this setup cripples the feature-based alternative, making fine-tuning appear superior due to an intentionally weak competitor, not its own inherent merit.
reasoning: The error describes a confounded experimental design where an extra variable (underpowered model) prevents the stated goal (isolating embedding power) from being achieved, which is explicitly listed as a characteristic of category D.
